In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column phrases are A, B, C and in the second column, the phrases are D, E, F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these' as your answer

Column(1) Column(2)
(A) We tried to capitalize on the customers' (D) latent dangers.
(B) They seriously believe that (E) curiosity to increase our gross sales.
(C)Many people say that detente  (F) ourselves from the masses
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A-E.

Key Points

  • Part A states 'We tried to capitalize on the customers' and part E states 'curiosity to increase our gross sales​'. 
  • In part A, the word capitalize means to take the chance to gain an advantage.
  • Here, it's said that they need to take advantage of the customers' curiosity regarding their products to increase their sales. 
  • There is only one correct combination in the given options i.e. A-E is the correct combination. 

The correct sentence is,  A-E:  We tried to capitalize on the customers' curiosity to increase our gross sales.

Direction: In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column phrases are A, B, and C and in the second column, the phrases are D, E, and F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select 'None of these' as your answer.

Column (1) Column (2)
(A) In ancient times, the sun was (D) incessant talking.
(B) Ageism is equally as offensive (E) an object of veneration.
(C) She became irritated by the child's (F) and pernicious as sexism.
questions.explanation:
The correct combination is 'B-F'.
Key Points
  • The correct sentences are:
    • A-E: In ancient times, the sun was an object of veneration.
    • B-F: Ageism is equally as offensive and pernicious as sexism.
    • C-D: She became irritated by the child's incessant talking.
  • Part A and part E should join conceptually. Part A states that 'In ancient times, the sun was' and part E states 'an object of veneration'. So, A-E is the correct combination.
  • Part B and part F should join conceptually. Part B talks about 'Ageism is as equally offensive' and part F completes the sentence stating 'and pernicious as sexism'. So, B-F is the correct combination.
  • Part C and part D should be joined conceptually. Part C talks about 'She became irritated by the child's' and part D completes the sentence stating 'incessant talking'. So, C-D is the correct combination.
  • The correct combination is reflected in option 4, making it the correct answer.

​

  • Let's look at the meaning of some difficult words:
    • Veneration: great respect; reverence
    • Pernicious: having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way
    • Incessant: (of something regarded as unpleasant) continuing without pause or interruption

Direction: In the following questions two columns are given containing three sentences/phrases each. Each question has five options. Choose the correct option in which the sentences/phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. 

I

II

 A. On account of space   limitations, magazine editors must

 D. display information when   you request information of it

 B. A terminal is any piece of   technology that will

 E. me away from the noisy streets of the city.

 C. The garden was an oasis of   calm that took 

 F. be selective in where they   place advertisements
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'A - F and C - E'.

Key Points

  • The phrases A - F and C - E when combined, form grammatically and contextually correct sentences.
  • B and D logically form a pair but D is grammatically incorrect. The phrase 'request information from it' is correct usage as it means that a terminal is any piece of technology that will display information when you request information from the terminal.
  • Therefore, all the options that contain D (options 2, 4 and 5), get eliminated.
  • Option 1 gets eliminated as C is talking about the garden and F is talking about placing advertisements.
  • Therefore, according to the given explanation, option 3 is the correct answer.

Direction: In the following questions two columns are given containing three sentences/phrases each. Each question has five options. Choose the correct option in which the sentences/phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. 

I

II

 A. I have to return the   software back to the store

 D. was independent and free from British control.

 B. After the revolution, the   colonies

 E. a youngster came along and grabbed his title.

 C. The boxer was an   undisputed champion until

 F. because it is not compatible with my computer.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'A - F and C - E'.

Key Points

  • The phrases A - F and C - E when combined, form grammatically and contextually correct sentences.
  • A is saying that the person has to give the software back to the store and F is talking about its reason.
  • C is talking about the boxer who remained an unopposed champion until a particular point in time and E has mentioned until when that boxer remained a champion.
  • B and D do not make a pair as the plural subject (colonies) should be followed by a plural verb (were) instead of 'was'.
  • Therefore, according to the explanation, option 4 is the correct answer.

A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If, none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these’ as your answer. 

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A)The small amount of water vapor in the Martian atmosphere suggests 

(D)only small amounts of carbon. 

(B) Ancient oceans on Mars contained 

(E)that there has been liquid water on Mars.

(C) The climate of Mars may not have been suitable 

(F)since the formation of large bodies of water.
questions.explanation:
The correct sentences are - 

  • A-E: The small amount of water vapour in the Martian atmosphere suggests that there has been liquid water on Mars.
  • B-D: Ancient oceans on Mars contained only small amounts of carbon. 

Key Points

  • We need to join each sentence part given in column 1 to their correct counterparts given in column 2. The sentences should not only be conceptually correct but also grammatically error-free. This would allow us to come to the correct solution.
    • Part A talks about a fact which provides a suggestion. Conceptually it should join with part E  which points out what this suggestion is. So, A-E.
    • Part B talks about oceans on Mars containing something. So, it should join with part D which mentions what it can contain. So, B-D.
    • Combining the rest of the parts do not make sense.
  • ​The correct combinations are reflected in option 4, making it the correct answer.

Important Points

  • Parts C and F cannot join.
  • Part C talks about how the climate on Mars is unsuitable for something. 
  • Part F talks about the period of time wit respect to the formation of the lakes. (By using 'since' as a conjunction.)

questions.text:
Direction: In the following questions two columns are given containing three sentences/phrases each. Each question has five options. Choose the correct option in which the sentences/phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. 

I

II

 A. The dog lover insisted  that her dog has

 D. easy locomotion and enables the   car to travels at high speed

 B. in the blizzard, many   highway travellers

 E. were searching for a haven from the freezing wind

 C. The rotary nature of fire allows for

 F. the capability to feel emotions just as humans do.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'A - F'.

Key Points

  • When the phrases A and F are combined, they form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. A is referring to the dog lover who is talking about her dog, and F is referring to someone who has emotions just like humans. As a result, it is possible to infer that the dog lover is insisting that his dog has emotions just like humans. 
  • D cannot make a pair with any of the phrases as it is grammatically incorrect. The verb after 'to' does not take any 's/es' form. ('to travel' is the correct usage)
  • C is talking about some rotary design of fire, and it does not make a suitable pair with any other phrases.
  • When we combine the phrases B and E, they give the meaning that many highway travellers were looking for a safe shelter from the freezing wind during the storm. They form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. 
  • Out of all the given alternatives, only in option 1, we have the correct pair i.e. A - F.
  • Therefore, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.text:
Choose the combination that creates the correct sentence.

A. Rajesh was still extremely angry

i. therefore

D. Mary having apologized a lot. 

B. Sam wanted to create a time machine

ii. despite of

E. she would miss her best friend's wedding.

C. Molly had to pack her bags really fast

iii. consequently

F. he had to study engineering.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B - i - F'

Key Points

 To choose the correct combination, we will have to go through all the options one by one. 

  • The combination 'B - i - F' i.e. 'Sam wanted to create a time machine therefore he had to study Engineering.' is correct because the second sentence is a consequence of the first. 
  • 'Therefore' is an adverb that is used to refer to a sequence of action, something happening as a result of an initial action. 
    • Example: Harry did not get into his dream college, therefore he had to settle for his backup college. 
  • The first part of the sentence tells us that Sam has a desire to create a time machine. In order to build this he has to take certain steps. 
  • The second statement tells us he had to study Engineering. This means that because he wants to create a time machine, in order to get the proper access to the knowledge for doing that, Sam had to study Engineering. 


Hence, the correct answer is 'B - i - F'.

Additional Information 

  • 'Therefore', 'consequently' and 'as a result' are connectors used to refer to causation in a sequence of actions. 
  • They usually appear in the middle of a sentence. 
    • Example: Markus failed the entrance exam, as a result he had to change his mind about becoming a doctor. 

                                     Jean wanted to buy a car, consequently she also had to learn how to drive.
